sections.title: Map the advertised service to your actual calls
paragraphs:

| Call population | Record your office needs | Confirmation for the contractor quote | Responsibility to retain |
|---|---|---|---|
| New residential inquiry | Contact details, service address and caller-described request | Which tailored form and delivery destination apply? | Decide whether the work is offered and approve any attendance promise |
| Existing customer update | Available reference, requested change and callback details | Is the service collecting a message or authorized to act on a booking? | Own the actual schedule change and unresolved request |

sections.title: Review the resulting record before accepting the scope
paragraphs:
Consider a fictional roofing office that wants customer inquiries delivered to its estimator while employee absence messages go to its manager. A single “take a message” instruction leaves important questions open: which form is used, who receives it and what the caller is told next?

Check that its purpose and recipient are clear, and that a request is not presented as an accepted appointment. If a live connection is part of the proposal, review the unavailable-recipient outcome separately. An attempted patch does not prove that an employee accepted the work.

Then request the commercial explanation for that exact scope: covered dates and hours, usage measure, additional work, later instruction changes and exit terms. Leave unknown figures blank rather than calculating a bill from an undefined meter.

record.title: Aspire Answering Service: Define the Staff Handoff
record.description: Evaluate Aspire's operator-to-staff messaging, delivery choices and account setup. Use a purchase worksheet to separate replies, messages and call logs.
record.lead: A message telling your office that somebody called is different from an exchange between an answering operator and your staff. When evaluating Aspire Answering Service, decide which interaction your business needs and have the proposed account explain how it works.
record.intro: A message telling your office that somebody called is different from an exchange between an answering operator and your staff. When evaluating Aspire Answering Service, decide which interaction your business needs and have the proposed account explain how it works.

sections.title: Identify the exchange you are buying
paragraphs:
[Aspire's service page](https://aspireansweringservice.com/answering_service.html) advertises interactive text messaging between its operators and the client's staff, alongside message delivery and call relay or patching. That supports asking about an operator-to-office exchange. It does not establish its timing, included usage or what the operator does when your employee does not respond.

For a fictional plumbing office, a caller might ask whether the business handles a particular fixture. The office may want an operator to record the question, or it may want an authorized employee to supply an answer. Those are different assignments. Neither should become a promised appointment or diagnosis without the office's approved instructions.

Aspire's [homepage](https://aspireansweringservice.com/) includes plumbers. Confirm your service area and call types separately.

sections.title: Use this interaction worksheet with the proposal
paragraphs:
The rows below are purchasing questions, not confirmed Aspire entitlements. Complete them with the supplier before relying on the arrangement. Use fictional details in an agreed demonstration.

| Decision | Answer to obtain | Evidence to inspect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entry mode | Live answering or the selected automated greeting and operator path | The actual caller experience for your configuration |
| Message to staff | Who receives the question and what information accompanies it | A sample message with the facts your office requires |
| Staff reply | Whether a reply is supported, who reads it and during which coverage hours | A demonstrated exchange under the proposed scope |
| Caller outcome | Whether the operator relays an approved answer, records a callback request or takes another agreed step | The resulting caller wording and office record |
| Unavailable employee | What happens when the selected staff member cannot respond | Written fallback instructions and remaining office responsibility |
| Commercial scope | Applicable unit, included work, additional charges and change process | The dated account proposal, not assumptions from a feature list |

A staff reply containing a preferred visit time does not itself reserve a crew. Identify who may approve a commitment and the wording used without approval.

sections.title: Separate immediate delivery from the later call log
paragraphs:
Aspire's [FAQ](https://aspireansweringservice.com/faq.html) lists several message-delivery choices and a call log supplied on specified days. Decide what your staff needs promptly and what the office reviews later. A scheduled log is not proof that somebody noticed an individual request or completed its callback.

Match the sample log to your office's follow-up record. Any required archive, retention period or export needs separate confirmation.

sections.title: Confirm the account and quote together
paragraphs:
The FAQ distinguishes a free local number from a toll-free option with a fee and describes an optional automated greeting leading to an operator. Its [plans page](https://aspireansweringservice.com/plans_and_pricing.html) describes customized arrangements without a numerical tariff in the reviewed text. Request the complete recurring and usage terms, including the selected number and any staff exchanges. Do not infer that a listed option is included in every quote.

Resolve account control and connection compatibility before changing your public number. Portability is not established here.

sections.title: Compare the work with Revo's verified scope
paragraphs:
[Revo's published plans](/pricing) list AI reception, appointment booking, SMS follow-up and dashboard summaries; team transfers appear on Crew and Fleet, not Solo. Confirm your supported connection and booking arrangement. These features do not establish interactive texting between a human operator and your employees.

If operator-to-staff exchanges are essential, evaluate a supplier that documents them and confirm the purchased behavior. If supported incoming AI reception and an office-reviewed summary meet the requirement, compare that narrower scope with Revo. No like-for-like saving is established here.

sections.title: Frequently asked questions
paragraphs:
### Does interactive texting mean the caller stays on the line?

The reviewed description does not settle that. Ask what happens to the caller while the office is contacted and what occurs when no answer arrives.

### Is an operator-to-staff exchange the same as answering customer texts?

No. They involve different participants and responsibilities. Confirm any incoming customer-text requirement separately.

[Compare Revo's current plans](/pricing) against the reception work your office actually needs and the responsibilities it will continue to own.
